project.name: my-browser-qute
project.description: my-browser — qutebrowser-based daily-driver browser with daemon-side integrations: FIDO2 passkeys via da_fido2-vault-broker, password autofill via da_autofill-rbw-rofi. Pure-config (no fork) — qutebrowser ships from nixpkgs; this project owns home-manager wiring + JSON-driven settings. Dir is da_my-browser; image name stays qutebrowser-standalone (release-pipeline identity); 'my-browser' is the display brand.

browser._default_browser_note: true → home-module sets xdg.mimeApps so qutebrowser owns http(s)/html/about/unknown scheme handlers (the system default browser). Flip to false to disown. Data-driven toggle read by src/nix/home-module.nix.
browser.comment: Upstream qutebrowser is configured via Python config.py OR via NixOS home-manager `programs.qutebrowser`. This project uses the home-manager path so the SoT is JSON + Nix, not imperative Python.

data_sources.comment: All four JSON files are read by the home-manager module at evaluation time and projected into qutebrowser's declarative options. Edit JSON, rebuild home-manager, browser picks up the new state.

release.comment: Standalone qutebrowser config bundle (config.py + quickmarks + bookmarks/urls + qute-bookmarks.html + --basedir launcher), independent of the ~6GB 37-module desktop home-manager closure. Built by `build.sh release` (nix build .#standalone), published to BOTH a GitHub Release (rolling tag, --clobber) and GHCR (oras, matching the repo's all-services-as-GHCR-images pattern) via `build.sh gh-release`/`build.sh ghcr-push`. install-standalone / the desktop flake pull from the GitHub Release ONLY — GHCR is a redundant/discoverable mirror, not a consumption path.

fork.comment: The my-browser (qute) FORK binary — patched qutebrowser (native bookmark + plugin chrome bar) packaged as a PORTABLE self-extracting executable via `nix bundle .#my-browser` (~640MB, QtWebEngine included, under GitHub's 2GB asset limit). Built by `build.sh fork-release`, published to its OWN rolling GitHub Release tag by `build.sh fork-gh-release`. This is the answer to 'deploy the fork in releases' — a single-file download that runs the fork without Nix. gzip'd for transfer.

fido2_vault_broker.comment: WebAuthn over /dev/hidraw — qutebrowser/Chromium auto-discovers the virtual FIDO2 device when the daemon is running. No extra config needed.

autofill_rbw_rofi.comment: Password autofill via global hotkey is OS-level (handled by da_autofill-rbw-rofi). qutebrowser sees the typed keystrokes like any other window.

vaultwarden_bitwarden_cli.comment: In-page autofill (Ctrl-Shift-B) via qutebrowser's OFFICIAL, in-tree qute-bitwarden userscript (qutebrowser/misc/userscripts/qute-bitwarden — ships bundled with the qutebrowser package, no vendoring needed). Uses the official `bw` CLI against our self-hosted Vaultwarden server (API-compatible with real Bitwarden). Matches by the vault item's saved URL (bw list items --url <domain>) — no need to rename entries. Session persisted via keyctl (keyutils), auto-locks after runtime.auto_lock_seconds. home.packages gets bitwarden-cli + keyutils; a home.activation step idempotently runs `bw config server <server_url>` (no secrets — the interactive `bw login` step is a ONE-TIME manual step, cannot be automated declaratively since it requires the master password).
